question.worked_solution:
We need to factor the following expression:

$$
-12{a}^{2}-6a+6
$$

First, notice that all the terms have a common factor of $-6.$ So, we can simplify the calculation by first factoring out $-6:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-6(2{a}^{2}+a-1)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we just need to factor the trinomial $2{a}^{2}+a-1$ in parentheses. To do this, we find two numbers that 

- multiply to the product of the quadratic coefficient and the constant (which is $2\times (-1)=-2$), and

- add to the linear coefficient (which is $1$).

The factor pairs of $-2$ are

$$
(1,-2),\,(-1,2).
$$

Notice the numbers in the factor pair $(-1,2)$ add to $1:$ 

$$
-1+2=1\,✓
$$

Then, we write the linear term as $-a+2a,$ and factor the result by grouping:

$$
\begin{aligned}2{a}^{2}+a-1 & = \\ 2{a}^{2}-a+2a-1 & = \\ (2{a}^{2}-a)+(2a-1) & = \\ a(2a-1)+(2a-1) & = \\ (a+1)(2a-1) & \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the original trinomial factors as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}-12{a}^{2}-6a+6 & = \\ -6(2{a}^{2}+a-1) & = \\ -6(a+1)(2a-1) & \end{aligned}
$$
